Hi Luca / Emma —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick follow-up based on the questions that came up on the call about what we actually store when you send prompts/queries to Redwood: I wanted to put our default behaviours in one place and propose a short action plan so your legal/security folks can review.

Summary (high-level):
- Default hosted API: transient request logs kept for 14 days; derivatives (embeddings/outputs) are NOT persisted unless you enable the "persist_outputs" or "save_session" flag.
- Dedicated instances: by default no cross-customer persistent derivatives are written; instance-local logs retained for 7 days unless you configure longer retention.
- Private / on‑prem: retention entirely customer-controlled; Redwood does not retain copy if you opt for Private with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).

Attachments: redwood_data_handling_one-pager.pdf (one-page matrix), healthcore-demo-notes.pdf (demo transcript)

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm whether HealthCore needs outputs stored by default (yes/no). If yes, we can propose a TTL and storage location (US/EU).
2) LegalOps: if you want a retention SLA we can map to our Dedicated offering (custom retention) — Karthik can follow up with options and pricing.
3) I'll loop in our Security team if you want an evidence package (SOC2 excerpts, logging schema).

If useful I can add explicit examples (API payloads with the flags) to the one-pager.

Thanks,

— Soojin

Hi Luca — great questions. Inline answers below.

> 1) When you say "transient request logs kept for 14 days" — does that include full prompt text or is that just metadata + anonymized traces?

Short answer: hosted API request logs include full prompt text by default for 14 days; we store them for debugging/quality monitoring. However, there are two features that address this:
- Data-Opt-Out: a tenant-level flag that prevents storing request bodies (you will see only metadata). This is enabled during onboarding for customers who require it.
- Redaction rules: we offer pre-processing hooks that can remove or mask sensitive fields before the request is recorded.

> 2) If we enable "persist_outputs" for a subset of calls, can we pin those persisted objects to a specific region (we need EU residency for some PHI-derived outputs)?

Yes. Persisted outputs can be stored in a chosen region (US, EU, APAC) as long as you select that region at the time of configuration. For Hosted customers this is a config option during tenant provisioning. For Dedicated/Private you control the storage endpoint (and in Private you can keep data entirely inside your VPC). Note: persisted outputs marked as "persist_outputs" are subject to the TTL you set (default 365 days for persisted outputs; can be shorter).

> Also, can you confirm whether cached KV data (prefix cache you mentioned) ever lands in persistent object storage, and if so what the TTL is?

KV/prefix cache: ephemeral in-memory cache for inference hot-paths — it is not written to persistent object store by default. For Dedicated customers, there is an optional persistent cache snapshot feature (opt-in) where snapshots are written to encrypted object storage; snapshot TTL is configurable and defaults to 30 days.

- Karthik will outline the Dedicated pricing delta for custom retention and region pinning.
- I will add examples to the one-pager showing the two data opt-out flows.

Hi Luca / Emma —

Quick note from pricing / enterprise side: we can deliver the following options for HealthCore's needs (summary):

1) Hosted standard: 14-day full-request retention (default). Option to enable tenant Data-Opt-Out during onboarding (no request bodies kept). No per-tenant persisted outputs beyond "persist_outputs" flag.
2) Hosted + retained outputs: Persisted outputs (TTL configurable) stored in selected region (EU option available). Base pricing increase + small per-GB storage fee. Default TTL on persisted outputs we propose: 365 days (adjustable).
3) Dedicated: instance-local logs with default 7-day retention; custom retention windows available (30/90/365+), region pinning included; add-on for encrypted persistent cache snapshots (30-day default).
4) Private: full control — Redwood control plane only; you manage retention and storage endpoints; we provide deployment and auditing support as part of the enterprise package.

If you want to move forward I can put together a short SOW (1 page) that lists the retention choices and estimated delta to the commitment.
